findings.explanation: high confidence.  Witness: For any smooth hypersurface with $\dim H_0^{n-1-i, i} = |I_i| > 1$ (e.g. a quintic threefold where $h^{2,1} = 101$, or a quartic surface where $h^{2,0}=1$ but for higher degree/dimension where components have dimension $> 1$), the space of classes $[y^{n-1-i} g(x)]$ has dimension $> 1$. The pairing $\mathcal{R}([y^i f_{j_i}], [y^{n-1-i} h]) = U_{k,\gamma}$ is a single linear constraint on $[h]$, which does not determine $[h]$ when $\dim > 1$. Furthermore, choosing an arbitrary $g_{j_i}$ with $r_{f_{j_i}, g_{j_i}} \neq 0$ forces $[\tilde{f}_{j_i}]$ to be a scalar multiple of $[g_{j_i}]$, which cannot equal the complex conjugate of $[y^i f_{j_i}]$ for two distinct non-proportional choices of $g_{j_i}$. Thus, (2.10) does not yield the complex conjugate in general and the proof in [p7-10] incorrectly asserts that finding the inverse image amounts to solving this single scalar equation with an arbitrary $g_{j_i}$.

findings.explanation: high confidence.  Witness: For any hypersurface where dim H_0^{n-1-i, i} > 1 (e.g. a quintic threefold where h^{2,1} = 101, or a quartic surface where h^{2,0} = 1 but h^{1,1}_0 = 19), the complex conjugate of a basis element is not proportional to an arbitrary chosen dual element g_{j_i}, so w_{j_i} is not real and the displayed span fails to give the real primitive cohomology (and moreover, the direct sum with R * sqrt{-1} w_j is closed under multiplication by i, contradicting that it is a real form). The correct construction of the real structure requires inverting the full Gram matrix of the pairing on H_0^{n-1-i, i} x H_0^{i, n-1-i} rather than a single pairing equation with an arbitrarily chosen element g_{j_i}(x).
